name: Rosa Luxemburg
role: Polish-German Marxist theorist and revolutionary (1871–1919), co-founder of the Spartacus League and German Communist Party
summary: Luxemburg was a revolutionary Marxist who argued that socialism must be won by the working masses' own action through mass strikes and councils, not by gradual reform or by a minority acting for them. She opposed war, militarism and colonialism as products of capitalism, rejected national self-determination as a socialist slogan, and criticised the Bolsheviks' suppression of civil liberties, insisting that freedom is always for the one who thinks differently.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Spartacus program replaces wage labour and commerce with planned production and distribution in the common interest, and Reform or Revolution treats capitalist production as anarchic.

public-ownership.rationale: Demands expropriation of banks, mines, smelters and large industry and commerce, and takeover of public transport by the council republic.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Demands confiscation of dynastic wealth and of all wealth above a level set by the central council.

unions-good.rationale: Calls trade-union work a 'labour of Sisyphus' that is nonetheless indispensable for securing wages, while insisting unions alone cannot end exploitation and stressing united action with the party.

property-fundamental.rationale: Her program makes the means of production the common property of all and expropriates large owners; the Reform or Revolution case treats capitalist ownership as the basis of class rule.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: her program calls for radical social legislation and a transformed health, housing and education system, so a call to cut welfare as harmful would run against it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Holds that the working collectivity alone should own all social wealth and that enterprise councils should take over the direction of enterprises.

strong-leader.rationale: Rejected rule by a handful of leaders in Russia as a Jacobin-style dictatorship and held that socialism cannot be decreed from above but must be made by the masses.

empower-police-military.rationale: Demands disarming the entire police force and abolishing officers' command authority; denounces militarism as a prop of ruling-class power.

decide-locally.rationale: Favoured broad local self-government without national privileges but argued capitalism centralises states and opposed federalism.

more-religion-public.rationale: Opposes public privileges for religion and attacks clerical use of the pulpit as a political weapon against workers.

gradual-change.rationale: Rejects Bernstein's gradual reformism and holds that legislative reform cannot replace the seizure of power.

nation-first.rationale: Holds that national interests serve only as a pretext for imperialism and that workers' interests are international.

revolution-justified.rationale: Argues in Reform or Revolution that the conquest of political power by revolution is indispensable to socialism.

central-planning.rationale: Calls for 'planned production and distribution of the product in the common interest' in place of the market.

socialized-markets.rationale: Her program abolishes contemporary commerce along with wage labour; she does not envisage markets between worker-owned firms.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Criticised the Bolsheviks' distribution of land to peasants as building up small property and class differences, and proposed socialist collectives instead.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: 'Down with the wage system' is the slogan of the hour in her program, and commerce is also to be abolished; money itself is not discussed separately.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rejected Bolshevik one-party rule: freedom only for government supporters is 'no freedom at all', and the Spartacus League says it will not seek power over the masses.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Welcomed the fall of the Hohenzollerns and demands abolition of all principalities.

democracy-best.rationale: Insists on general elections and free opinion in a socialist state and calls council rule 'true democracy', while rejecting bourgeois parliamentarism as class rule.

workers-councils.rationale: Wants workers' and soldiers' councils to replace parliaments and municipal councils from the top of the state to the parish.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposed the Bolshevik slogan of a right of separation as a gift to border-state counter-revolution; backed autonomy rather than separation.

political-violence-never.rationale: Holds the bourgeoisie will resist and that its counter-revolutionary violence must be met with revolutionary violence, in what she calls the mightiest civil war in history.

war-builds-character.rationale: Describes the First World War as mass slaughter and the suicide of the working classes of Europe.

separate-church-state.rationale: Demands abolition of public privileges for believers over unbelievers and opposes the Church becoming a dominating power in the state.

military-superiority.rationale: Treats armaments competition as a product of imperialism and militarism, and rejects 'national interest' as a pretext for it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Treats class struggle as the driving force of history and the basis of the socialist movement, invoking the Communist Manifesto.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Names egotism, stupidity and corruption as the moral foundations of capitalist society and public spirit as that of socialism.

direct-action.rationale: Championed mass strikes as the key revolutionary weapon, yet urged using elections and parliament as platforms against them.

means-match-ends.rationale: Holds that socialism must be built by the masses' own activity and democratic self-discipline, not by decree, but accepted revolutionary violence and dictatorship over former rulers.

production-for-use.rationale: Contrasts capitalist exploitation with planned production and distribution in the common interest, with labour as everyone's social duty.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Defends Marx's law of surplus value against Bernstein and says reform must aim at ending, not merely reducing, exploitation by the wage-labour system.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Defines the arming of the working masses with all political power as 'the dictatorship of the proletariat' and 'true democracy'; in Russia she insisted it be a class dictatorship, not a party's.

collective-farming.rationale: Calls for socialist agricultural collectives on expropriated large and medium estates, with small peasant holdings left until their owners join voluntarily.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Junius Pamphlet traces the First World War to imperialist rivalry among capitalist classes.

total-state.rationale: Insists socialist life needs the masses' free self-direction, and warns that bureaucracy alone remains when public life is stifled.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Analyses imperialist expansion and colonial seizure as the cause of war and condemns it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Proposes enterprise councils that regulate working conditions, control production and finally direct the enterprise.

national-self-determination.rationale: Called the right of nations to self-determination hollow, petty-bourgeois phraseology and a Bolshevik error, arguing there is none under capitalism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Denounces the SPD's wartime civil peace and its collaboration with the bourgeoisie, and refuses to join government with Ebert and Scheidemann.

workers-nation.rationale: Ends the Junius Pamphlet with the call 'Proletarians of all lands, unite' and attacks the SPD for placing the nation above the international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Her program demands complete legal and social equality of the sexes.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Describes the present state as first of all an organisation of the ruling class, though she says this should be understood dialectically.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Her council republic expropriates industry, directs production and reshapes education and housing, far beyond defence and justice.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Demands legal and social equality of the sexes, abolition of rank and titles, and rejects any national privilege.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Ties the Russian and German revolutions to world revolution and says lasting results require the international proletariat.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Says the Spartacus League will take governmental power only on the clear will of the great majority of the proletarian masses.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Endorses forcible expropriation and revolutionary violence against resisting ruling classes while saying the revolution itself hates killing.

separated-powers.rationale: Makes the central executive council the highest organ of both legislative and executive power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed Lenin's centralism, arguing the party is the proletariat itself and that blind obedience to a central committee cannot replace the masses' self-direction, though the Spartacus League describes itself as the most conscious part of the class.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Criticised terror and suppression of democracy under Bolshevik rule as damaging the revolution, though she backed disarming the ruling classes in her own program.

party-controls-media.rationale: Criticised the Bolsheviks for outlawing press freedom and the rights of assembly for opponents.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Accepted 'self-discipline' within the party but rejected blind obedience to a central committee.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Calls a 'United States of Europe' contrary to the course of economic and political development.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rejects supporting her government in war and calls for class struggle against it, but holds that either 'defeat' or 'victory' is a defeat for socialism.

recall-officials.rationale: Provides for immediate recall at any time of council delegates and of officers elected by their units.

people-in-arms.rationale: Argues for replacing standing armies with an armed people's militia, and her program arms the adult proletariat.

minority-language-support.rationale: Backs schools in minority languages and use of those languages in local administration and courts, by an empire-wide language law.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Argued that under capitalism each class of a nation determines itself differently, so national freedom is empty without socialism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Criticised Lenin's dissolution of the Russian Constituent Assembly and called for fresh elections, but in Germany called the National Assembly a counter-revolutionary stronghold.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Supported Poland keeping its own legislature and administration within the Russian state while sharing common state affairs.

land-redistribution.rationale: Wants large estates expropriated, but criticised the Bolsheviks' seizure and division of land among peasants as non-socialist and as sharpening class differences.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Called non-territorial national autonomy, for example for Jews, a utopian construction 'fluttering in mid-air', and opposed separating workers by nationality.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Argues for the materialist conception of history, grounding the case for socialism in capitalism's economic development, and faults Bernstein for abandoning it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Describes self-discipline, public spirit and social duty, not the capitalist whip, as the moral basis of socialist labour.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rejects Blanquist insurrection by a small conspiratorial minority; revolution must come from the great majority of the masses.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Demands abolition of all differences of rank, orders and titles and of all principalities.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Describes colonial rule as forcible seizure of land and labour from other societies; footnotes the Herero and Putumayo atrocities as examples.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The chapters on capitalism's adaptation and its collapse reject Bernstein's claim that credit, cartels and communications let capitalism avoid general crisis.

elective-rulers.rationale: Calls for abolition of all principalities and a united socialist republic with elected councils.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Argues capital accumulation depends on seizing and exploiting non-capitalist territories and peoples through colonial policy, loans and militarism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Wants officers' authority abolished, officers elected and recallable, and counter-revolutionary officers excluded from the soldiers' councils.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Demands that councils' delegates be subject to immediate recall by those who elected them.

single-official-language.rationale: Endorsed an official language alongside minority languages in schools and local administration, and quoted the Austrian party's rejection of a state language.

informal-organisation.rationale: Argued for a mass party growing out of class struggle and open public life, and opposed conspiratorial groups.

religion-illusion.rationale: Says the religion of the masses will disappear only along with present society, when people consciously direct social processes.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rests women's claim to equal rights on their role as wage-earners and ties it to the proletarian class struggle rather than bourgeois feminism.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Argues co-operatives are a hybrid form within capitalism that cannot be the means of transforming society.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Frames the choice as 'socialism or barbarism' and founded the German Communist Party; she offers no third course.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Wrote that 'freedom is always freedom for the one who thinks differently' and that without press and assembly freedom public life dies out.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Demands complete freedom of conscience and the widest toleration for every faith and opinion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Her account of colonial policy denounces plunder of colonised peoples and land for European capital.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Says the working mass must make political and economic life its own and run it consciously and autonomously, in workplaces and councils.

social-market-economy.rationale: Argues social reform and labour legislation cannot turn capitalism into socialism and that a programme of reforming capitalism abandons the final aim, though reforms remain tools of struggle.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Replaces the professional army with an armed workers' militia rather than disarming entirely.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Her program abolishes principalities and confiscates dynastic wealth.

property-franchise.rationale: Her mass-strike writings and election articles fight the Prussian three-class franchise and demand universal equal suffrage for both sexes.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Says Social Democracy does not fight religious belief and demands complete freedom of conscience.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Her program ends the monopoly of a class over the means of production, so that 'hunger' falls on idleness rather than on labour and a decent life goes to those who do their social duty.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Calls for arming the people to defend the revolution against counter-revolutionary attack.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Holds that socialism can be built only by the working class's own action and that councils must hold all power.

arms-reduction.rationale: Condemns militarism but calls partial limitation of armaments an impracticable half-measure under capitalism; she looks to socialism to end it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Calls for disarming the police and ruling classes and arming the workers as a militia and Red Guard, not leaving arms to state forces.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Calls for replacing parliaments and councils of the old order with workers' and soldiers' councils; cites the Paris Commune lesson that the working class cannot simply take over the ready-made state machinery.

workers-own-party.rationale: Built workers' parties her whole career (the Polish SDKPiL, the SPD left, the Spartacus League and KPD) as the class's own organisations.

women-suffrage.rationale: Gave a speech demanding equal political rights for proletarian women and called the lack of women's suffrage a prop of reaction.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defends the Russian Revolution against German and Allied counter-revolutionary intervention and credits the Bolsheviks with historic achievement while criticising them.

indirect-election.rationale: Her scheme has local councils elect delegates to a central council, which elects the executive council.

national-church-status.rationale: Calls for abolition of all public privileges enjoyed by believers and no public money for churches.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Backed autonomy for the Kingdom of Poland within a democratic Russia, where Poles were a clear majority, but rejected it for Lithuania, the Caucasus and elsewhere.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Defends Marx's law of value and surplus value as the core of economic theory against Bernstein.

notes: Positions come mainly from her own writings (1893-1919). On the Russian Revolution she praised the Bolsheviks' seizure of power while criticising their dissolution of the Constituent Assembly, press restrictions, land distribution and slogan of national self-determination. On means she accepted revolutionary violence and class dictatorship but rejected terror and one-party rule. Her 1918 Spartacus program is her latest statement of aims. Her 1899 argument for a militia and her 1905 speech on churches are read as her mature views.
